content.text:
The pattern fits a cubic double perovskite, and the superstructure peak intensities point to Sr2FeBiO6 (mp-1205525). I located peak positions by counting grid points, so they are approximate to a few tenths of a degree.

- **Observed peaks:** about 18.4° (24%), 30.6° (100%), 36.0° (38%), 37.8° (20%), 43.9° (29%), 45.5° (14%) and about 54.5° (13%).
- **Double-perovskite fit:** the conventional cubic cell is a ≈ 8.217 Å (primitive 5.81 Å × √2). It predicts reflections at 18.7° (111), 30.75° (220), 36.2° (311), 37.9° (222), 44.05° (400) and 54.7° (422). These match the observed set well.
- **Spinel rejected:** CaV2O4 (a ≈ 8.92 Å) would put strong peaks at about 28.3° and 33.3°. Those positions are flat in the observed pattern.
- **Choosing between the two double perovskites:** Sr2FeBiO6 and Ba2MgMoO6 have almost identical cells (8.217 vs 8.212 Å), so peak positions cannot separate them. Intensities can, because the odd-index superstructure peaks (111) and (311) scale with the scattering contrast between the two B-site cations.
  - In Sr2FeBiO6 that contrast is Bi vs Fe (83 vs 26 electrons), which is very large.
  - In Ba2MgMoO6 it is Mo vs Mg (42 vs 12 electrons), and the main peaks are also dominated by heavy Ba.
  - The observed (111) at about 24% and (311) at about 38% are strong, which favours Sr2FeBiO6.
- **Second phase:** a weak bump near 33° may be noise or a minor second phase. It is not strong enough for me to assign a second candidate.
